nodes.description: White Tiger Legacy. Details: The Delhi Zoo was a pioneer in breeding White Tigers; all white tigers in zoos today descend from a single cub named Mohan.
The Dancing Deer. Details: The Sangai deer (Brow-antlered deer) is called the "Dancing Deer" because of its delicate gait on floating islands in Manipur.
Painted Stork Hub. Details: Every August hundreds of wild Painted Storks migrate to the zoo's islands to nestâ€”one of North India's largest natural colonies.
Mughal Heritage. Details: The zoo is built on the 16th-century Citadel of Indraprastha grounds right next to the historic Purana Qila (Old Fort).
The Kos Minar. Details: An original 16th-century Mughal-era "Kos Minar" (mileage pillar) still stands perfectly preserved inside the zoo grounds.
Rhino Armor. Details: The Indian One-Horned Rhino has skin that looks like a suit of armor but it is actually sensitive to insect bites and sunburn.
The Ghara. Details: Male Gharials (crocodiles) at the zoo have a "Ghara" (pot-shaped bump) on their snout used to blow bubbles during courtship.
Asiatic Lion Fold. Details: Unlike their African cousins the Asiatic lions in Delhi have a distinctive longitudinal fold of skin running along their bellies.
Friday Rest Day. Details: The Delhi Zoo is strictly closed every Friday to give the animals a full day of peace and quiet from human visitors.
Hippos Blood-Sweat. Details: Hippos secrete a red oily fluid called "blood sweat" that acts as a natural antibiotic and sunblock for their skin.
Jaguar Patterns. Details: While they look like Leopards Jaguars have "rosettes" with small spots inside the ringsâ€”a unique jungle fingerprint.
Elephant Memory. Details: The zoo's Indian Elephants can recognize themselves in mirrorsâ€”a rare sign of high intelligence in the animal kingdom.
Sloth Bear Vacuum. Details: Sloth bears can close their nostrils voluntarily and use their gap-toothed snouts like high-powered vacuums to suck up termites.
Blackbuck Speed. Details: The Indian Blackbuck is one of the fastest land animals in India reaching speeds of up to 80 km/h to escape predators.
Royal Bengal Stripes. Details: No two Royal Bengal Tigers have the same stripe pattern; their skin is also striped just like their fur.
Peafowl Pride. Details: The Indian Peafowl is our National Bird; a male's "train" can contain over 200 shimmering feathers with colorful eye-spots.
Chimpanzee Tools. Details: Chimpanzees at the zoo are known to use sticks as tools to "fish" for insects showing incredible problem-solving skills.
Himalayan Bear V. Details: The Himalayan Black Bear has a distinctive white "V" or crescent shape on its chest earning it the name "Moon Bear."
Emu Eggs. Details: Emus lay large dark green eggs that look like polished emeralds; it is the male emu who incubates them for 8 weeks.
Nilgai Height. Details: The Nilgai is Asia's largest antelope; its name literally means "Blue Bull" due to the bluish-grey coat of the adult males.
Leopard Stealth. Details: Leopards are the strongest climbers among big cats and can carry prey twice their weight high up into trees.
Python Strength. Details: The Indian Rock Python is a non-venomous constrictor that can go for months without eating after a single large meal.
Sambar Ears. Details: Sambar Deer have massive ears that rotate independently like satellite dishes to detect the slightest sound of a predator.
Mugger Durability. Details: Mugger Crocodiles have existed for millions of years; their name "Mugger" comes from the Hindi word 'Magar' meaning monster.
Ostrich Eyes. Details: An Ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain; they are also the only birds that have just two toes on each foot.
Zebra Stripes. Details: Zebras use their stripes as "motion dazzle" to confuse biting flies and predators while they move in a herd.
Gaur Power. Details: The Indian Gaur is the largest wild cattle species in the world; a full-grown male can weigh over 1000 kilograms.
Barking Deer. Details: The Indian Muntjac is called the "Barking Deer" because it lets out a loud dog-like bark when it senses danger.
Cormorant Diving. Details: The Little Cormorant seen in the zoo ponds is a master diver that can stay underwater for over 30 seconds to catch fish.
Cassowary Danger. Details: The Southern Cassowary has a 5-inch dagger-like claw on its inner toe making it the world's most dangerous bird.
Brahminy Kite. Details: In Indian mythology the Brahminy Kite is often identified as 'Garuda' the sacred mount of the God Vishnu.
Chinkara Water. Details: The Chinkara (Indian Gazelle) can survive for long periods without drinking water by getting moisture from plants.
African Elephant Ears. Details: You can tell the African Elephant apart by its ears which are shaped roughly like the continent of Africa.
Great Hornbill. Details: The Great Hornbill has a huge yellow "casque" on top of its beak which acts as a hollow chamber to amplify its calls.
Indian Wolf. Details: The Indian Wolf is a master of endurance; they are known to trot for miles without tiring while tracking prey.
Star Tortoise. Details: The Indian Star Tortoise has a shell pattern that helps it blend into the tall dry grasses of the scrub forests.
Pelican Pouches. Details: The Rosy Pelican can hold up to 13 liters of water in its throat pouch which it uses like a fishing net.
Macaque Society. Details: The Lion-tailed Macaque is one of the most endangered primates; it lives in complex social groups led by a dominant male.
Hog Deer Height. Details: The Hog Deer gets its name from its habit of running through the forest with its head down like a wild hog.
Swamp Deer Hooves. Details: The Barasingha (Swamp Deer) has splayed hooves that prevent it from sinking into the soft mud of marshy areas.
Jackal Intelligence. Details: Golden Jackals are highly adaptable and have been known to follow tigers to scavenge the remains of their kills.
Red Junglefowl. Details: The Red Junglefowl found in the zoo is the primary wild ancestor of all the domestic chickens in the world today.
Spotted Deer. Details: Also known as 'Chital' these deer never lose their white spots even as they grow into adulthood.
Hyena Laugh. Details: The Striped Hyena doesn't actually "laugh" like its African cousin but it makes various chattering sounds when excited.
Porcupine Quills. Details: An Indian Crested Porcupine's quills are actually modified hairs; it can rattle them to warn off curious predators.
Green Lung. Details: The Delhi Zoo's 176 acres host over 5000 trees providing a vital "green lung" that purifies the city's air.
Wildlife Library. Details: The zoo has a dedicated library on site with thousands of books about birds animals and Indian wildlife history.
Azimganj Sarai. Details: The zoo's first animals were kept in the ancient Azimganj Sarai a Mughal rest house for travelers from centuries ago.
Conservation Breeding. Details: The Delhi Zoo participates in a global program to save endangered species like the Asiatic Lion from extinction.
Zoo School. Details: The National Zoological Park offers internship programs for students to learn about veterinary care and animal behavior.
Flamingo Filters. Details: Flamingos are filter feeders; they use their specialized beaks to strain small organisms from the water while upside down.
Indian Cobra Hood. Details: The cobra spreads its hood by extending its long ribs; the "eye" pattern on the back is meant to scare away predators.
Gibbon Song. Details: Hoolock Gibbons are the only apes found in India; they are known for their loud melodic "songs" used to mark territory.
Turtle Longevity. Details: Some turtles in the zoo's reptile house can live for over 100 years outlasting many human generations.
Night Heron Eyes. Details: The Black-crowned Night Heron has large red eyes that help it see clearly in low light while hunting at dusk.
Goral Climbers. Details: The Himalayan Goral is a goat-antelope that can easily navigate near-vertical cliffs in its mountainous home.
Eurasian Spoonbill. Details: The spoon-shaped bill of this bird is highly sensitive to touch helping it find prey in murky water without seeing it.
Civet Scent. Details: The Asian Palm Civet has a scent gland that produces a musky secretion used to mark its nocturnal path.
Leopard Rosettes. Details: Unlike a Jaguar's spots a Leopard's rosettes are empty in the middle without a central spot.
Golden Pheasant. Details: The male Golden Pheasant has a spectacular golden crest and bright red body making it one of the most beautiful birds.
Rat Snake Speed. Details: The Common Rat Snake is non-venomous and incredibly fast; it is often mistaken for a Cobra because of its size.
Sand Boa Tail. Details: The Indian Sand Boa has a tail that looks like a second head to trick predators into attacking the wrong end.
Monitor Tongue. Details: Monitor lizards use their forked tongues to "smell" the air just like snakes do to track their prey.
Budgerigar Mimics. Details: Budgerigars (Budgies) are small parrots that are actually capable of learning and mimicking hundreds of human words.
Zebra Finch Song. Details: Male Zebra Finches learn their unique songs from their fathers; no two males sing exactly the same tune.
Lady Amherst. Details: Named after the wife of a Governor-General of India this pheasant has a 3-foot long silver and black tail.
Sarus Crane Height. Details: The Sarus Crane is the world's tallest flying bird standing at a height of nearly 6 feetâ€”almost human size!
Egyptian Vulture. Details: This intelligent bird is known to use rocks as tools to crack open thick-shelled ostrich eggs in the wild.
Silver Pheasant. Details: The male Silver Pheasant is known for its bold white and black plumage and bright red face patch.
Red-and-Green Macaw. Details: These large parrots use their powerful beaks to crush even the hardest nuts and can apply 2000 pounds of pressure.
Hanuman Langur. Details: Known as the "Sacred Langur" in India they are protected by local people and are seen living near temples.
Bengal Fox Ears. Details: The Bengal Fox has exceptionally large ears relative to its body size which help it dissipate heat in hot weather.
Macaque Pouches. Details: Macaques have cheek pouches that allow them to store as much food as their stomach can hold for eating later.
Flying Fox Wings. Details: The Indian Flying Fox is one of the world's largest bats with a wingspan that can reach up to 4 or 5 feet.
Otter Socializing. Details: Smooth-coated otters found in India are highly social and are often seen playing and grooming in family groups.
Darter Snake-Bird. Details: The Darter is called the "Snake-bird" because its long thin neck looks like a snake when it swims underwater.
Pied Kingfisher. Details: This bird is famous for its "hovering" technique where it stays perfectly still in mid-air before diving for fish.
Yellow-Wattled Lapwing. Details: This bird prefers dry open ground and is known for the bright yellow fleshy "wattles" in front of its eyes.
Crimson Barbet. Details: Also known as the "Coppersmith Barbet" because its repetitive call sounds like a hammer hitting copper metal.
Indian Hoopoe. Details: The Hoopoe has a spectacular crest of feathers that it fans out when it is excited or alarmed.
Golden-Backed Woodpecker. Details: This woodpecker has a specialized "shock-absorber" skull that protects its brain while it hammers on trees.
Parakeet Nesting. Details: Rose-ringed parakeets often nest in hollow tree cavities or even in holes in old buildings inside the zoo.
Sun Parakeet. Details: These small South American parrots are famous for their brilliant yellow and orange "sunset" colored feathers.
Blue-and-Yellow Macaw. Details: These birds can live for over 50 years and are known to be extremely loud and social in their jungle homes.
Cockatiel Crest. Details: A cockatiel uses its crest to express its mood; vertical for excited flat for angry and slanted for relaxed.
Zebra Finch Beak. Details: A Zebra Finch's beak color can tell you its gender; males usually have bright red beaks while females have orange.
Great Horned Owl. Details: These owls have "ear tufts" which are not ears at all but feathers used for communication and camouflage.
Black Swan Neck. Details: The Black Swan has the longest neck of any swan allowing it to reach deep underwater to find tasty plants.
Rhea Flightless. Details: The Greater Rhea from South America is a large flightless bird that uses its wings like rudders to turn while running.
Kalij Pheasant. Details: The Kalij Pheasant is often found in the thick undergrowth of Himalayan forests where it stays hidden from predators.
Spotted Owlet. Details: These small owls are often seen in pairs sitting on tree branches during the day while they sleep.
Barn Owl Silent. Details: The Barn Owl has special "fringed" feathers that allow it to fly in absolute silence while hunting at night.
Koel Rainy Season. Details: The Asian Koel is most vocal during the Indian monsoon season; it is a brood parasite that lays eggs in crows' nests.
Crow Pheasant. Details: Also known as the Greater Coucal this bird has bright copper-colored wings and a deep booming "oop-oop" call.
Pied Crested Cuckoo. Details: Legend says this bird only drinks raindrops; its arrival in North India is seen as the official start of the Monsoon.
Palm Swift. Details: These tiny birds build their nests on the underside of palm leaves using their own sticky saliva as glue.
Green Bee-eater. Details: This bird is an expert at catching bees in mid-air; it rubs the bee against a branch to remove the stinger before eating.
Indian Roller. Details: The Indian Roller is the state bird of several Indian states; it gets its name from its spectacular aerial acrobatic displays.
Blue-throated Barbet. Details: This bird lives in the upper canopy of the forest and is hard to see despite its bright green and blue colors.
Yellow-fronted Woodpecker. Details: This small woodpecker is easily identified by the bright yellow patch on its forehead and its black and white stripes.
